relevance_note: Pictorial imaging review that describes several identifiable patients with an ATS diagnosis (e.g. 'Case 1: 7-month-old female child with poor weight gain and suspected cardiac disease was diagnosed with ATS.'), but prints no SLC2A10 variant for any of them.
method_note: Read in full by hand; the JSON was assembled with a short Python script from hand-chosen values and spans, all checked verbatim against the paper. The paper is a pictorial essay based on 17 patients; individuals are described only in figure legends. Rows were made for the three labelled cases (Case 1, Case 2, Case 3) and for four unlabelled males whose legends give a distinct age/sex/presentation (Figures 20, 21, 24, 26 -> unnamed person 1-4 in order of first mention). Unlabelled legends whose description is word-for-word identical to a labelled case were NOT given separate rows and their findings were NOT attributed to that case: '4-month-old female with dysmorphic features and abnormal echo' (Figures 5, 12b, 19b; same wording as Case 3) and '1-month-old female with prenatal suspicion of cardiac disease' (Figure 9b; same wording as Case 2). The four unlabelled males (three are 4-month-old males: Fig 20 'abnormal facial features and cardiomegaly', Fig 24 'feeding difficulty and failure to gain weight', Fig 26 'abnormal facial features and failure to thrive') may partly be the same person; they were kept apart because the paper does not say so. Ages are the ages given in each legend (age at the illustrated examination) and were recorded as age at last evaluation, not diagnosis. No SLC2A10 variant is printed and no variant is tied to any individual, so the variants table is empty; the text says the illustrations come from sporadic cases and from 'the cohort of patients with mutations in the SLC2A10 gene' [refs 2,5] without saying which patients carry variants, so n_patients_reported and cites_prior_report_of_same_patients are null. Cohort-level statements (consanguinity in 'one cohort of patients', one death from cardiac failure, one hiatus hernia repair, one prenatal detection) are not attributed to any individual. Table 1 and Table 2 have no content in the converted text. Narrowing: Case 1 SMA 'multiple focal narrowing' and Case 2 aortic 'significant luminal narrowing' were counted as stenosis of the aorta or aortic branches; Case 1 'relative narrowing of proximal parts of right and left pulmonary arteries' was not counted as pulmonary artery stenosis (the paper contrasts relative narrowing with 'significant stenosis'). Cardiomegaly / left ventricular cardiomegaly was not counted as ventricular hypertrophy; diaphragmatic eventration (unnamed person 4) was not counted as hernia; 'Lungs are unremarkable' (unnamed person 1) is a whole-organ normal finding recorded as written and excludes nothing more specific. No contradictions found.
